diseases.name: Soybean Rust
diseases.description: Asian soybean rust: a fast-spreading rust fungus that can strip soybean fields of their leaves.
diseases.causes: Spores blow long distances on the wind; leaf wetness of 6+ hours at 15-28 °C lets them infect. The fungus does not survive cold winters.
symptoms: Small tan to red-brown spots, starting on the lower leaves
Volcano-shaped pustules on the underside releasing tan spores
diseases.effect: Rapid leaf loss cuts pod fill and yield.
diseases.untreated: Unchecked epidemics can cause heavy yield losses.

steps.title: Scout the lower leaves
steps.instruction: Check the undersides of lower leaves with a hand lens.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide as soon as rust is found on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Fungicides work best before much leaf area is lost.

steps.title: Follow regional warnings
steps.instruction: Track rust reports from your region.

lifecycle: Spores blow in from warmer regions.
They infect leaves wet for several hours.
Tan lesions with pustules form underneath.
Millions of new spores spread up the field.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: bean rust

diseases.name: Bacterial Blight
diseases.description: A bacterial leaf spot of soybean in cool, wet weather.
diseases.causes: The bacteria survive in residue and seed and spread by wind-driven rain into the leaves.
symptoms: Spots turn dark brown with a yellow-green halo
Spots merge; dead tissue tears out, leaves look ragged
diseases.effect: Usually minor; severe cases reduce yield.
diseases.untreated: Ragged leaves in cool, wet years.

steps.title: Note the extent
steps.instruction: Check how much of the upper canopy is affected.
steps.rationale: Most outbreaks fade in warm weather.

steps.title: Avoid working wet fields
steps.instruction: Stay out of the field while leaves are wet.

steps.title: Plan rotation and clean seed
steps.instruction: Rotate and use clean seed next season.
steps.rationale: Residue and seed carry the bacteria.

lifecycle: Bacteria survive in residue and seed.
Wind-driven rain splashes them onto leaves.
Water-soaked spots turn brown with halos.
Dead tissue falls out.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: soybean bacterial blight

diseases.name: Brown Spot
diseases.description: Septoria brown spot: the most common leaf spot of soybean, starting on the lower leaves.
diseases.causes: The fungus survives on residue; rain splashes spores onto the lowest leaves in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small, irregular dark brown spots on lower leaves
Leaf tissue round the spots turns yellow
diseases.effect: Lower leaves drop; yield effect is usually small.
diseases.untreated: In wet seasons it climbs the plant and reduces yield.

steps.title: Scout the lower canopy
steps.instruction: Check how far up the plant the spots reach.
steps.rationale: Only spread to the upper leaves matters.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide if spots climb past mid-canopy on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: The fungus overwinters on residue.
Rain splashes spores to the lowest leaves.
Brown spots with yellow surrounds form.
It climbs the plant in wet weather.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: soybean brown spot
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Downy Mildew
diseases.description: A water-mould disease of soybean leaves, pods and seed.
diseases.causes: Spores survive in residue and on seed; cool, humid weather lets them infect.
symptoms: Pale yellow-green spots on the upper leaf
Grey to purple tufts of spores underneath
Spots turn brown with yellow margins
diseases.effect: Usually minor; seed can be infected.
diseases.untreated: Heavy infection causes early leaf drop.

steps.title: Scout the leaf undersides
steps.instruction: Look for grey tufts in the morning.

steps.title: Use treated, clean seed
steps.instruction: Use seed free of the disease.

lifecycle: Spores survive in residue and seed.
Cool, humid weather lets them infect.
Pale spots form with grey tufts underneath.
Pods and seed can be infected.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: soybean downy mildew
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Frogeye Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of soybean with round, grey spots ringed in red-purple.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on residue and seed; warm, humid weather spreads them by wind and rain.
symptoms: Round spots, 1-5 mm, with grey to tan centres
A dark red-purple ring round each spot
Spots on the upper, younger leaves
diseases.effect: Spots reduce the leaf area; leaves can drop.
diseases.untreated: Severe infection reduces yield; fungicide resistance is common.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide (check local resistance reports) on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on residue and seed.
Warm, humid weather spreads spores.
Grey spots with purple rings form.
Spots join and leaves drop.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: soybean frog eye leaf spot
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Soybean Mosaic
diseases.description: A virus disease that mottles and puckers soybean leaves and mottles the seed.
diseases.causes: Spread in infected seed and by aphids that pick it up from infected plants within seconds.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic on young leaves
Leaves puckered, crinkled and curled down
Plants stunted; seed coats mottled brown
diseases.untreated: Infected seed carries it into the next crop.

steps.title: Mark infected plants
steps.instruction: Note where mottled, stunted plants are.

steps.title: Remove early infected plants in small plots
steps.instruction: Pull out mottled plants while they are few.

steps.title: Use virus-free seed next time
steps.instruction: Buy certified seed or resistant varieties.

lifecycle: Infected seed gives infected seedlings.
Aphids carry the virus to nearby plants.
Young leaves mottle and pucker.
Seed from infected plants is mottled.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: soybean mosaic
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.
